Table 1. Null GWAS simulation

Null GWAS (no true effects, 100 replicates). LD-fit loss is the excess Gaussian loss (ridge 0.001) of each method's LD matrix over the mixed matrix at the generating weight; lower is better. Null score variance is the variance of target-sample scores relative to EUR-only PRS-CS for the same GWAS. Chromosome 22, fixed 250 kb LD blocks; the GWAS combines EUR and ASN discovery samples at 70:30. PRS-CS with automatic φ. Means over replicates with Monte Carlo standard errors in parentheses; within a replicate every method analyses the same simulated GWAS and scores the same target individuals. PRS-MIX at w = 1.0 and 0.0 is identical to EUR-only and ASN-only PRS-CS. The seed rerun repeats EUR-only PRS-CS with a different sampler seed and measures run-to-run variation. *Generating weight.

Table 2. Non-null GWAS simulation

Non-null GWAS (sparse causal effects shared across ancestries, 100 replicates). Top-10% overlap is the share of target individuals in a method's top score decile who are also in EUR-only PRS-CS's top decile; correlation is between their scores. r2 is the squared correlation between scores and true genetic values. Chromosome 22, fixed 250 kb LD blocks; the GWAS combines EUR and ASN discovery samples at 70:30. PRS-CS with automatic φ. Means over replicates with Monte Carlo standard errors in parentheses; within a replicate every method analyses the same simulated GWAS and scores the same target individuals. PRS-MIX at w = 1.0 and 0.0 is identical to EUR-only and ASN-only PRS-CS. The seed rerun repeats EUR-only PRS-CS with a different sampler seed and measures run-to-run variation. *Generating weight.

Table 3. Replicate-paired differences against the seed rerun

Replicate-paired differences, each method minus the EUR-only seed rerun, with the standard error of the paired difference in parentheses. Every quantity is first measured against EUR-only PRS-CS, as in Tables 1 and 2, so the differences show how far a method moves scores beyond what a new sampler seed alone does. Negative overlap and correlation differences mean larger changes than run-to-run variation; pp, percentage points. *Generating weight.
